reading.body:
Lovo is a voice cloning and synthesis company whose only listed product is Genny, and the data records no data center, power, or compute footprint for it at all.

The profile is a single product entry: voice cloning and synthesis, likeness consent, commercial voiceover, synthetic media disclosure. That is a description of what the software does and what rules it carries, not of what it runs on. The one attached MCP server, ai.lovora/lovora, describes a different subject entirely, an 18+ AI companion service, and the only thing tying it to this record is the name.

For AI specifically, voice synthesis is an inference workload, and inference workloads are the part of the stack most directly priced by compute and electricity. A company in this category competes on latency, concurrency, and cost per generated second, all of which move with the price of GPUs and power. None of that appears here. The record does not say where Lovo trains or serves models, whether it owns or rents capacity, or how much of its cost is compute.

What the data does not tell the reader is nearly everything about scale. There are no funding figures, no customer counts, no usage numbers, no dates beyond the generation timestamp, and no cases. The alias list contains only the company's own name. Treat this as an identity and product record, not as evidence about Lovo's position in the compute supply chain.
